utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. For the Prosecution this morning, Mr. President, Matthias Neuner, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, Daryl Mundis, and we are assisted by Mr. Andres Vatter, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Muriel Cauvin, legal assistant, thank you..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber would like to greet everybody on this Friday morning. We would like to greet the Prosecution, the Defence teams, the accused, and everybody else in the courtroom. I'm going to ask Mr. Registrar to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We resume in open session. We shall continue the testimony of the witness by the examination-in-chief of General Kubura. I would kindly ask the usher to bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. While the witness is coming in, in light of the comments that Your Honour just made, it does raise an interesting issue whether this witness is appearing as a joint Defence witness for Mr. Kubura, in which case it would be examination-in-chief, or whether they consider him to be not one of their witnesses, so that they would be cross-examining him. And of course that might make a difference on whether -- the treatment that they're giving the witness in terms of the questioning, and we would simply ask that be put on the record, whether they consider this to be a joint Hadzihasanovic and Kubura Defence witness or whether the Kubura team does not consider him to be one of their witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, bearing in mind what my learned friend has just said, General Merdan is not a joint witness, so we shall cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. That was a question that I have had in mind for several weeks now. This question has not been raised so far, but if the witness is a joint witness, obviously you conduct examination-in-chief. If it is not a joint witness, then you will cross-examine him. General, I hope you had a nice rest, because your testimony will continue today. At the beginning, you will be answering questions put to you by the Defence team of General Kubura. They have indicated to us that they will need about two hours. After that, it will be the Prosecution who will conduct their cross-examination in chief. Obviously this will last throughout the following week. This is more or less how your testimony will proceed. I'm going to give the floor to the Defence team of General Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you several questions on behalf of General Kubura's team. They will be relative to your testimony over the past three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little mistake in the transcript in line 11. I believe that questions should be addressed to General Merdan, not to General Kubura. I believe that this was a mistake in translation. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Than you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, during your testimony, you were talking about the establishment of the 7th Muslim Brigade. You said that when you were talking about the reorganisation of the corps and the establishment of brigades within the 3rd Corps. The 7th Brigade was established in November 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we will be using some documents during our examination, with your permission I'd like the witness to be shown these documents. We have provided copies for the Trial Chamber as well as for all the other participants in this hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, can you please look at document number 1 and document number 2. The first document is P124. This is a letter or a request that you sent to the Supreme Command Staff on the 18th of December, 1992. You drafted this document and you signed it yourself. Have you been able to find it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In the second line here, it says: "These forces number about 1.200 soldiers, armed, equipped, and ready to fight." You're referring to the Muslim forces. Your request to the Supreme Command Staff was to use these men for the establishment of the 7th -- of the 7th Muslim Brigade. How come that you sent such a letter to the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that the situation was very complex following the occupation of Jajce. In Travnik and in the Vlasic plateau, the situation was very difficult and very complex. As the commander of the regional staff at the time, I faced a number of problems. First of all, I had to stabilise the defence line, and I was not successful in that. The aggressor kept on advancing. There were a lot of refugees. The population that joined from the region of Kraula, they were volunteers whom I could not put under control since the aggressor kept on advancing. The territory of Kraula also fell and the Chetnik, that is aggressor, came very close to Travnik. I have a lot of problems with men. I could not stabilise my defence line. I engaged all of my troops, and after a very difficult period of time, I managed to stabilise the line and I could see that there were a lot of people from Krajina who were not organised. They Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond expressed their willingness to fight but they had not been organised up to then. Together with my personnel from the staff, I estimated that there were about 1.200 men there. That is why my proposal was to establish a new unit, the 7th Muslim Brigade, to unite all these men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: These men, the 1.200 men that you have mentioned both in your testimony and in your letter, they were all Bosniaks, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. And it was my assessment that there were about 1.200 of them. I don't know whether they all wanted to join the brigade, however, this was my estimate, and I thought that a written request is -- was due in order to establish such a brigade. Those people hailed mostly from Krajina, from the territory that had already been occupied by the aggressor. They wanted to fight, but I did not find any other means to organise them for fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at document number 2. That is P125. This is an order of the Supreme Command Staff. In this order, you can read under item 1, organisational preparations, under one formation: "From a Mountain Brigade under the name of the 7th Muslim Brigade from the RBH army, from the brigade, in accordance with the temporary wartime establishment," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So the 7th Muslim Brigade was established pursuant to this order?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You know, Mr. Merdan, that the command of the 7th Brigade was in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the command of the 7th Muslim Brigade was in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion was established in Travnik, the 2nd in Zenica, and the 3rd in Kakanj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When the brigade was being established -- actually, when the 2nd Battalion was being established in Zenica, the people who joined this battalion was the population of Zenica and the surrounding area. When the Kakanj battalion was being established, it was composed of the population from the region of Kakanj and the surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The 7th Muslim Brigade was replenished on the territorial principle from almost all the municipalities. So these battalions were formed with the population from those areas, as you have just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When the 1st Battalion was being established in November 1992, it had about 300 men. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be more or less the number, 300 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, I shall put it to you and -- that some officers of the 306th brigade were here as well as the commander of the 227th and the 312th Brigade were here. They told us that some of the fighters from the Vlasic plateau joined some other units, not only the 7th Muslim Brigade. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that there were about 1.200 men in the area who could be organised into a unit. We could not put all of these units into only one brigade. Some other brigades were formed at the same time, and these men were then assigned to the other brigades as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the number of 1.200 men, and if you know that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, which was in Travnik, was the -- was the 7th Muslim Brigade, then most of the men went to other brigades.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. I said that I had information that certain groups called themselves Muslim forces, that they fought the aggressor in the area, but these Muslim forces, as they called themselves, were not on the strength of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And obviously only parts of these forces joined the 7th Muslim Brigade. The rest of the men joined other brigades. I assume that the group that called itself Muslim Armed Forces, or the MOS, which was the customary abbreviation for them, was spread across several brigades in the area, one of them being the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In your request to the Supreme Command Staff, you only used the term "Muslim forces," not MOS.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that there was a lot of propaganda and different names were used. I did not have, on the strength of the Territorial Defence, a unit of that kind, and I just went along with the rumours. I could not know exactly what forces were in question, whether they were Muslim forces or MOS. So this does leave room for mistakes, because at the time, there were a lot of rumours; I did not have the precise information at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, can you please look at document number 3, which is the Prosecution number 192. The English version is at the beginning. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The report of the command of the 3rd Corps, and the date is August 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim Brigade, as a brigade of the 3rd Corps, was established as an independent brigade, according to this report. Can you look at page 0 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found the page: 01051603.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that within the 3rd Corps, which is composed of three operative groups, there are four independent brigades; the 314th, the 303rd, the 301st, and the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: One can see in this report that the 7th Muslim Brigade relied for the logistics of -- relied on the logistics of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was on the strength of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at page number -- the page speaking about the replenishment of the brigade. The number is -- the last three digits are 604. Several pages after the one that you have just had a look at.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the replenishment of units, you can see that the 7th Muslim Brigade was replenished up to 76 per cent of its full strength.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You look at the replenishment status of some other units. For example, the 3rd; the 304th Brigade, the 302nd Brigade from Visoko, the 306th Brigade, the 308th Brigade from Zavidovici are better replenished than the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. The 7th Muslim Brigade was the only brigade within the 3rd Corps which was known as a Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, do you know if there were other brigades within other corps that were known as Muslim Brigades? I'm just going to mention some of them that we found in the documents of the Sarajevo police. Within the 5th Corps, there was the 101st Muslim Infantry Brigade. The 1st Podrinje Muslim Brigade, the 1st Muslim Brigade of the 1st Corps, the 4th Muslim Brigade, the 17th Muslim Brigade, 241 Sprecanska Infantry Brigade, and 242nd Muslim Zvornik Brigade. Are you aware of all this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had information that in other territories under other corps, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina army, there were other Muslim brigades. I've already said that this was not the first time the word "Muslim" is used as part of a brigade name. This was the case during Austro-Hungarian Empire, during the Second World War. There were Muslim brigades then. So this is nothing new in the history of this part of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. During your testimony, you were also talking about religious practices in the BiH army, and if I understood you well, you said that unlike in the former JNA, the BiH army allowed its troops to Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond express their religious beliefs and practice their religion.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, and that's what the case was in practice. We did not prohibit the expression of religious feelings irrespective of the religion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document. The Exhibit number is P122.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This document was drafted by the Ministry of Defence and regulates the issues of religion in the army.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document. The exhibit number is -- it's a new document, actually, and the origin is the Sarajevo collection. This document was drafted by the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an instruction to Muslim fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On religious practices at defence lines outside of urbanised areas and under specific circumstances.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. This is a 3rd Corps document which was signed by Mr. Serif Kadric, the assistant commander for moral guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This document was sent to all the units of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to all the fighters within the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is the instruction to Muslims with regard to practising their religious beliefs under specific conditions.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, you have just told us that the command of the 7th Brigade was in Zenica. Do you know where the seat of the military police of the 7th Brigade in Zenica was?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the music school in Zenica, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I received information that the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade had been established, I also received information that it was headquartered in the then-music school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the music school and the headquarters of the military police of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I visited the headquarters of the military police was when we received information that the 7th Muslim Brigade kept prisoners of war and that they were kept by the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade. This was the first time that I ever went to the music school where the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade was billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get there on your own or did you go with representatives of the international community or with an officer from the 7th Brigade or with someone else?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time was with representatives the international community, because the international community said that prisoners were being kept there and that we weren't aware of that. I went there together with representatives of the international community, and on that occasion we didn't see any prisoners of war on the premises -- on the premises of the 7th Muslim Brigade. After that, I went there on two to three other occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find anything unusual there? Did you notice anything unusual?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went there on the first time with the representatives from the international community. Well, after this visit, we continued to receive complaints about prisoners being held in the music school. I wanted to verify that information. At the time, I thought that these were just rumours that were being spread. I went there later with a policeman who escorted me, but on that occasion, I didn't find any prisoners of war there either. I informed the international community of the fact that I had visited the premises and that I hadn't seen any prisoners of war there. Obviously the international community wasn't satisfied. They had other information. I thought that perhaps something was being concealed from me. On one occasion I went there without having announced myself. Again, even on that occasion, I didn't find any prisoners of war there. As I have said, I went to the premises of the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade on several occasions, but I really didn't see a single prisoner of war there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Was that in 1993, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everything that I've referred to occurred in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you had noticed anything unusual, you would have probably informed the brigade command or you would have asked the brigade command for some sort of an explanation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. If I had noticed anything unusual, anything particular, if I had seen that there were prisoners of war there and that we in the corps command weren't aware of the fact, in such a case we would have reacted. I would have asked the brigade commander to draft a detailed report and to inform the brigade command of the measures that had been taken. I've mentioned this on a number of occasions. The corps command issued clear instructions on the way in which prisoners of war were to be treated. We controlled the way these orders were being implemented. These orders reached the brigades. I would have asked for a detailed report from the brigade commander if I had noticed that there were any prisoners of war there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I'd now like to move on to another subject that you testified about yesterday in the course of your examination-in-chief. I'd like to move on to the events in Miletici. Please have a look at documents number 7, 8 -- 6, 7, and 8.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've had a look at those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think you saw these documents yesterday.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday in the course of your testimony, you said that after you found out about the events in Miletici, you visited the place on the 25th of April, 1993. That was one day after the events in Miletici.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That was my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: As you said yesterday, you received information about how individuals were killed in Miletici.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I was testifying about yesterday. That's what I knew, and I mentioned information I had, and I mentioned what I myself observed in Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You received information in Miletici, or in Mehurici, from inhabitants who were there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I was quite precise. I said the first information I received was at a meeting of the joint commission in Vitez, and then I went to the scene, and after I had returned from the scene in Miletici, on my way back - this was on the road - Franjo Nakic and I got out of the personnel carrier and met a group of local people there. They weren't in the village, they were on the road. And those local people who were there - later we found out that they were from Miletici, there were Croats and Muslims among them - these people, these Croats and Muslims, told us about what had happened in Miletici. So I wasn't in either of the villages or, rather, I didn't find out about what had happened in either of the villages. I mentioned that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The information you received at that time and subsequently shows that members of the BH army didn't participate in those events.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what the inhabitants of that village said. They said that only the Mujahedin had taken part in those murders. I didn't know who the Mujahedin were then. Yesterday, I told you when I first meet a group of foreigners whom they called the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that you also met a local commander of the BH army in respect to him.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I asked whether there was anyone present, a soldier said he was the commander. I don't know his name, but he said he was the local commander. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't a member of the 7th Brigade, this commander?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He said he was a member of the 306th Brigade and not of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't notice the presence of soldiers of the 7th Muslim Brigade on that road?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Miletici there weren't any soldiers and there weren't any inhabitants either. I noticed that there were a few soldiers with a group of people on the road, five or six of them. I can't remember how many exactly, but there were five or six of them who were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't notice a single officer from the 7th Brigade when you saw those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see a single member or single officer of the 7th Muslim Brigade. I said that the local commander said that he was a member of the 306th Mountain Brigade, and I believed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: No one told you that the 7th Brigade was in Miletici a day before, and the commander from the 306th Brigade didn't confirm the presence of members of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no information [Realtime transcript read in error "I had information"] according to which one day earlier there were members of the Muslim Brigade in the village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think there may be an error in the transcript. Page 16, line 22. It says "I had information", and it should say "I had no information." "I didn't have any information on the presence of members of the 7th Muslim Brigade in Miletici."

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I had no information that there were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade one day earlier in the village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you have a look at the documents we have been referring to, P576, Osman Tahirovic is mentioned here, Vahid Jasarevic, Lutvo Malanovic, Osman Tahirovic. In P561, Senad Vukovic is mentioned, Jasmin Jasarevic, then Osman Tahirovic again, Esref Prcanovic, Edin Colo. In P687, Osman Tahirovic, Jasmin Jasarevic, Tahir Jasarevic, Sabahudin Koric, Kasim Jasarevic. These names appear in this document. These are names of local people who were somehow involved in the events in Miletici. I assume that these names don't mean anything to you, General.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know these people. I don't know who they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to suggest that on the basis of the evidence we have on the members of the 7th Brigade none of these men were ever members of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about that. I knew brigade commanders and some battalion commanders, but I didn't even know who the company commanders were let alone the platoon commanders. How would I know the soldiers in brigades? There were a lot of soldiers, there wasn't much time. People rotated very rapidly and brigade commanders were frequently replaced. I wasn't able to know the names of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I'd now like to move on to the events in Maline. You testified about these events yesterday. Have a look at document number 9, please, P174. This is your report dated the 21st of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I referred to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In this report, it says in the combat in Maline, members of the 306th Brigade and armed inhabitants took part who were not members of the BH army. And at the end it says that the assistant commander from the 306th Brigade was on the site and compiled a report which he sent to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I drafted this report on the basis of the reports that I received from subordinate commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Before this report, there was a request from the 3rd Corps Command dated 17th of October, 1993, to the commander of the Bosnian Krajina Operations Group to forward information from subordinate units on the events in Maline. This is document number 10.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and I testified about this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The basis of your report is the reports you received from subordinate units or, rather, the Operations Group for Bosnian [Realtime transcript read in error "Kosovo"] Krajina and information you received from the 306th Mountain Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And yesterday, I also said that at the beginning of August, I was at the site with a mixed delegation, European Monitors and Mr. Stipe Radic. So in August, I had personal knowledge of the situation because I was up there as a member of that mixed commission. I saw the location of those two gravesites, and I've testified about this in detail yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at document number 11. On page 18, line 15, it should say the Operations Group Bosnian Krajina, and not the Operations Group Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says Krajina here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was mentioning -- I was referring to the transcript, but please have a look at the document. Have you found document number 11?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report from a military unit of the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: From October 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen this document. This report was the basis upon which you drafted a report that you sent to your superior command, a report that had to do with the events in Maline?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a new document. The Defence obtained this document when going through the archives of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, in order to compile this report which you sent to the superior command, the Operations Group Bosnian Krajina and subordinate units had information on the identity of those who participated in the operation around the village of Maline and on how the operation finished; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at document number 12. It's also a new document. It's a war diary from the 3rd Corps, an excerpt from the war diary, and it's from the Sarajevo collection. That's the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I briefly rise to my feet simply to indicate that it might be preferable for these new documents to be given some kind of number, even if it's just for identification purposes, to keep the transcript a little bit cleaner. There have been a number of documents with tab numbers, and clearly the tab numbers will be meaningless as we review the transcript in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Does the Defence object to giving these new documents and only the new documents numbers for identification as you will be tendering these documents into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objections, but we can make a list of the new documents during the break, and this might make it easier for all of us when it comes to tendering these documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the document dated 19th of October, 1993, was shown to General Merdan in the course of his examination-in-chief, and it is also in the list of documents that Defence counsel will be tendering into evidence. So when a list is being compiled, just try to make sure that we don't tender the same document into evidence twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The document dated the 19th of October had the number 1418 [as interpreted], but the problem is if the other Defence team wants to tender this document into evidence as well, because the interests of both teams might not be identical.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Our document is 1498, not 1418, which is what it states in the transcript. We have nothing against Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond the Defence requesting that they tender this document into evidence. We have no problems with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 22, it's not 1418; the document number is 1498. As far as document 1498 is concerned, dated the 19th of October, could we have a number for that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar would prefer to have the list during the break so that we don't get confused. We'll wait until the break for the list. Please continue. For the moment, everyone is following. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We're referring to document number 12, an excerpt from a war diary of the 3rd Corps. This is also a new document which we will be including in the list that I'll provide after the break. General, have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you have a look at the date, 5th of June, 1993. It says 1/7, the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was engaged in the direction of Hajdareve Njive.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Hajdareve Njive is?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know where that location is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Hajdareve Njive is in the immediate vicinity of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It's to the east of Travnik, right next to the town of Travnik itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the next document, number 13. It's also a new document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. The Judges can't find the reference you mentioned. You said in document number 12, at the bottom of the document, reference is made to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Brigade. Which page is this on?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the second page in the English translation. It first mentions the 312th Brigade engaged against the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. Yes. In fact, in English it says that 1/7 Muslim Mountain Brigade is engaged in Hajdareve Njive. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We were talking about document number 13, which is also a new document. It's a interim combat report from the command of the Bosnian Krajina Operations Group, dated the 5th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've managed to find the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 2, when it says "our forces," reference is also made -- again it says the 1st Battalion of the 7th Brigade was engaged towards the direction towards Hajdareve Njive, and it was being covered by its mortars.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found that. It's similar to the record in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In document number 12, we had an excerpt from the operations diary of the 3rd Corps, and this is an interim report from the Bosnian Krajina Operations Group. And their information as far as the battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade is identical; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, let's have a look at document number 14 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is also a new document which was also on the list of Mr. Hadzihasanovic's Defence, and Mr. Kubura's Defence wants to use this document too. I will we deal with this issue during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found this document, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. This is a report and suggestions from the Bosnian Krajina Operations Group forwarded to the command of the 3rd Corps. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This report mentions the problems that you talked about, the problems that the 306th Brigade had, and you can see that the commander of the 306th Brigade was ordered to organise a unit, the strength of one battalion with 300 combatants out of parts of the 306th Brigade and out of inhabitants from Mehurici, and he was to go in the direction of the Maline-Krpeljici-Bukovica. Have you found that part?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, could we now have a look at document number 15. It's also a new document. It's a war diary from the 306th Mountain Brigade. The source of this document is the Sarajevo collection. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the date, the 7th of June, 1993? The 306th Brigade was organised, and units, available units from the 306th Brigade were to participate in the action that we have already spoken about in the village of Maline sector.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I'd now like you to have a look at P465, dated the 8th of June, 1993. It's a regular operations report from the command of the Bosnian Krajina Operations Group. A witness who has already testified here said that this was General Alagic's handwriting. At the bottom you can see that it says that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade - and the date is the 8th of June - was to take action at the Hajdareve Njive feature and in the direction of Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In item 3, it says that the 306th Mountain Brigade was the only one that engaged in military operations on that day.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This was on the 8th of June, 1993, at 1900 hours. This was processed at 1945 hours. General, can you please look at P579, under number 17 in your binder. This is a telegram of the 306th Brigade sent to the 3rd Corps Command, in which it says: "We are currently under line Maline, Guca Gora, Mosor, Velika Bukovica." The date is 8 June 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have this document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When we compare the previous document, the report written by General Alagic and the telegram drafted by the 306th Brigade, we can see that the information in the Bosanska Krajina OG is identical.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at document number 18. This is a new document, and it was found in the archives of the BiH army. Again, this is a telegram of the 306th Brigade sent to the command of the 3rd Corps on the 9th of June, 1993. At the end of the telegram, it says: "Yesterday, our forces reached the line of villages Maline, Guca Gora, Mosor, Velika Bukovica." And this was drafted on the 9th of June, 1993. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, since you have had a look at all of these documents and we have analysed them together, could you agree with me that these documents, all of them, show what the situation was in the field? Do they also show that members of the 7th Muslim Brigade were not involved in the combat operations on the 8th of June in the Maline village sector?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on all of these reports drafted by subordinate units, one can conclude that this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, the documents that you have just had a look at are all relevant and were probably used both by the Bosanska Krajina OG and the 306th Brigade when they were sending this report based on which you drafted your report on the events in Maline that you sent to your superior command. I believe that these reports were relevant.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they should have been relevant. However, at that time I did not have an occasion to compare any of the reports. I just received the reports that we asked for. But basically I can now see that Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond this was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, I shall put it to you that before this Trial Chamber we had a witness called General Reinhardt. He is an expert. And when my colleague Mr. Dixon was examining this witness, his question to the witness was that, according to the documents that General Reinhardt had at his disposal, he was certain that the 7th Brigade was not involved in the events in Miletici and it wasn't involved in the military operations in Maline. General Reinhardt confirmed that. Can you now agree with my statement that you, based on the information that you had at the time and subsequently, did not find any evidence of the presence and participation of members of the 7th Brigade in Miletici and Maline in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I fully agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony, you have mentioned the developments in Kakanj at the beginning of June. You mentioned the dates the 9th, 10th, 11th of June, and you mentioned that the intense fighting had already started in the area of Kakanj at that time.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I testified to that effect. According to our information, the incidents already started on the 8th, and they escalated into an armed conflict on the 10th and 11th of June, of course.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the 2nd and 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade were engaged in the combat operations in Prevoja and Ovnak in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that fact. A tactical group was established at the time, if my memory serves me right, and the 2nd and the 3rd Battalions of the 7th Muslim Brigade were engaged in that Tactical Group. They came from Zenica via Ovnak towards the Bila valley, and I've already said something about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 2nd and 3rd Battalions were engaged in operations only up to the Ovnak pass, and they cooperated with some other units of the 3rd Corps, such as the 314th Brigade and others.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A tactical group was formed. It was a mixed tactical group. I did not mention all the units that formed it. The 2nd and the 3rd Battalions of the 7th Brigade were tasked with lifting the blockade off Ovnak in order to make the road to the Bila valley passable. That is because the 306th Brigade was in a very difficult situation. They asked for assistance, and I testified to that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 2nd and 3rd Battalions of the 7th Muslim Brigade, at the beginning of conflict in the area of Kakanj, found themselves in Kakanj. They had returned from Ovnak pass, and they participated in the operations to liberate Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. When the operation around Ovnak was finished, then the 2nd and 3rd Battalions of the 7th Muslim Brigade were sent to Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The situation at the Ovnak pass was stable on the 8th of June, and you confirmed that you were there on that day, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I was up there very briefly. I personally saw that the Ovnak sector had been liberated. I, however, said that there were still fightings west to Ovnak or south-west to Ovnak. There were still skirmishes but Ovnak itself was freed. It had been liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The 2nd and the 3rd Battalions of the 7th Brigade, on the 10th and 11th of June, 1993, left this area, the area around Ovnak. Kindly look at the documents marked by 21 and 22 in your binder. Document number 21 is a new document. The source of this document is the Sarajevo collection. Were you able to locate this first document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The date is 10 June 1993, and it is a plan of commander's reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This document shows that this is a plan of commander's reconnaissance which was drafted by the assistant, Safet Junuzovic. It was approved by Commander Kubura, the date is 10 June, and this plan is relative to the Kakanj sector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One can conclude that based on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the following document, under 22, this is a new document again, and its source again is the Sarajevo collection. You can see that -- have you got it, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is an order for attack dated 11 June 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This order is relative to the combat activity of the 7th Muslim Brigade in the Kakanj sector.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, having looked at these two documents, can you tell us whether these two documents confirm that the 2nd and the 3rd Battalions, on the 10th of June and the 11th of June, 1993, were deployed in Kakanj in order to participate in combat there?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the second document, at the last page of this document, under number 14, when the words "Command and communications" are mentioned. It says: "The brigade command post in Zagradje village sector will commence work at 2200 hours on the 11th of June, 1993."

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Since the order refers to the operations carried out by the 7th Muslim Brigade in the Kakanj sector, Zagradje village is very close to Kakanj, or in Kakanj municipality, which is clear from this document, because it would be logical for a command post to be in the zone where the operations are taking place.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we have managed -- mentioned the village of Zagradje, can you please look at document number 23. This is an order of the command of the 7th Brigade to train recruits in the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Brigade. Have you got it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You've already told us that the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was deployed in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Look at item 5. "The commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade shall inform the commander of the 309th Mountain Brigade and the commander of the Kakanj Municipal Staff of the execution of this order."

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got that and this is exactly what it says under this item.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 309th Brigade was based in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the Kakanj Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 1, you can see that one company of the 3rd Battalion shall be deployed to the village of Zagradje.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When we look at this document, which is P564, the village of Zagradje, where one company of the 3rd Battalion was being trained, is the place where the command post of the 7th Muslim Brigade was during the operations in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff, since you were the commander of the regional defence staff, you are also aware of the existence of the municipal defence staff in Kakanj, and it existed, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it existed in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The municipal defence staff of Kakanj could exist and could carry out operations only in the territory of the municipality of Kakanj. There is no way it could undertake any other activities or carry out any Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond operations in any other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. It is a territorial unit which covered only the territory where it was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dzemal. General, you were the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. At the beginning of November 1993, did you hold that position, the deputy corps commander?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November 1993, I was still the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of November 1993, while you were in that position, a very important military operation was taking place to liberate Vares; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document under 24. This is P217.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I signed the document on behalf of Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment he was no longer the commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the transitional period. He was being transferred to another position, and the new commander was being appointed. So this was the hand-over period. I know that after this, General Hadzihasanovic left the 3rd Corps. This was the hand-over period, and I signed the document. We had still not received the order on the appointment of the new commander. However, I knew that it was on its way from the Main Staff of the Supreme Command. That's why I signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the 7th Muslim Brigade was involved in the military operations to liberate Vares? And this is clear from the order that you signed.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I prepared this order based -- pursuant to the order of the Supreme Command staff for the engagement of the 7th Muslim Brigade in the territory of the municipality of Vares in order to liberate the municipality of Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document, which is under number 25. This is P47 -- 487. The date is 4 November 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have found the document, and this is a report on the engagement of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. In the combat operations around Vares, units of several corps were engaged.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that other corps were also taking place in those operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You're referring to the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at document number 26, which is P449. Have you had a look at it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report of the 3rd Corps Command. The date is 8 November 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by Commander Mehmed Alagic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim Brigade, according to this report, was late for the operations in Vares. They had transportation problems from Zenica to Breza, so they were late by one day.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have noticed that in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Given the situation that this brigade was late, according to some reports the 7th Muslim Brigade entered the town of Vares or came to its very entrance without a bullet fired. It had not engaged in any fighting. By that time, the combat operations had been over.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In the town of Vares, General, there was no fighting. There were no combat operations?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the units of the HVO withdrew from the town of Vares without a bullet fired. They did not engage in fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when the units of the BiH army and units of the civilian police entered the town of Vares, many buildings in the town of Vares were damaged, torched, and this was done by the Croatian Defence Council when they were abandoning the town.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard such reports. However, at that moment I was not in Vares, and I did not see all those things. I only knew about that from reports. I personally didn't see any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, General, that in addition to the 7th Muslim Brigade, there were some other units of the BiH army in the town of Vares as well as members of the municipal defence staff of Vares and also members of the 2nd Tuzla Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can speak only based on the reports. There were a lot of units there as far as I know. A special technical group had been established. There were several units there. There were also units of the 2nd Corps, because the combat operations were carried out on the axis towards the 2nd Corps as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the report of the command of the 3rd Corps, dated the 13th of November, and let's look at line 5. And the date on the report is 8 November.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that document number 25?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's 26. The report that we have just looked at, signed by General Alagic. "When we arrived in Vares, looting started." Did you find that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In his report, Commander Alagic says that due to the quick intervention of the military police of the Istok Operations Group, the 7th Muslim Brigade and the Ministry of Interior, this was stopped.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, do you know that the commander of the 7th Brigade ordered to all the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade to enter the town of Vares? Can you please look at document number 27 in this binder.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the commander of the 7th Brigade forbade members of the 7th Muslim Brigade to enter the town and to stay there?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any such order. I only know that brigade commands in all of their orders forbade looting and plunder. I know -- I know that there were such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found this document under 27?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at it when you find it.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that troops are not allowed to enter Vares and stay there without the commander's approval.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the first item in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, after this order, all members of the 7th Brigade who were found in Vares were lined up, and they had to leave the brigade. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that information, but I was not there and I didn't witness that. However, I did know of this order, and I was aware of this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And now the last document in this binder. This is P450. You will find it under our number 28.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is the document dated 17 November 1993 by the armed forces Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by the deputy commander, General Jovan Divjak.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You can see in this document that the minister of the interior has sent a document which says that on the 16th of November, 1993, a unit of the 2nd Corps, about 300 troops, entered the city of Vares, and that after Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond the arrival of that unit, individual cases of stealing and looting began.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read that in the first paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This document was sent to the commands of the 2nd and the 3rd Corps, and General Divjak asked for all these things to be prevented and that measures should be taken against the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to point out that the date is the 16th of November 1993. That's when the unit entered Vares, but the date of the document is the 17th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: A minute ago I showed you some documents. Now I suggest that the 7th Muslim Brigade left the town of Vares on the 6th of November, 1993, as early as that date.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the reports that I had, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General, for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this concludes our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It's half past ten. We will now have our technical break, and we'll resume at about five to eleven. When we resume, General Kubura's Defence will tell us what they intend to do with the documents and whether they have compiled their list of new documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume. I'll give the floor to Mr. Mundis, but before I do so, there are documents that Defence counsel has to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have compiled a list and provided it to everyone. There are nine new documents, and we have mentioned the source for each of these documents, and we'd like to tender these nine documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, any comments with regard to this list of nine documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution has no objection to the nine documents being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar -- any objections that the other Defence team would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the sake of the transcript, I would like to say that we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But that was understood. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are nine documents that will be admitted into evidence. The first one D416, the English version D416. Its title is "Instructions for Muslim Soldiers." The date is the 9th of February, 1993. I'll correct the transcript: It's DK16. The second document, DK17. The English version DK17/E. Its title is "Information," and the date the 19th of October, 1993. The third document will be DK18, and the English version DK18/E. Its title is "War Diary." The date, the 5th of June, 1993. The fifth [as interpreted] Document will be DK19, and the English version DK19/E. The title of the document "Extraordinary Combat Report," dated the 5th of June, 1993. The fifth document will be DK20, and the English version DK20/E. The title of the document is "Report and Proposal" and it is dated the 5th of June, 1993. DK21 will be the number for the sixth document, and the English version DK21/E. The title of the document is "War Diary" and the ERN number is 01826763. The seventh document will be DK22, and the English version DK22/E. The title of the document is "Telegram," and it is dated the 9th of June, 1993. The eighth document will be DK23, and the English version DK23/E. The title of the document is "Plan of Commander's Reconnaissance," and it is dated the 10th of June, 1993. And finally, document number 9 will be DK24, its English version DK24/E. The title of the document is "Order For Attack," and it is dated the 11th of June, 1993. That concludes the list of documents, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. As we're dealing with the documents, I'd like to take this opportunity to address General Hadzihasanovic's Defence. In the course of the examination-in-chief, you provided us with the three binders. In these binders we noticed that there were some documents which have already been admitted into evidence and there are others that you showed to the witness and asked him to identify them, and it was your intention to tender them into evidence, perhaps not all of them but some of them. So would you be able to make a new list for us including the documents that you want to tender for next week. You can disclose this to the Prosecution, too, and this will make it easier for everyone to keep track of the documents, and it will make it easier for the registrar to give the numbers. This shouldn't take long and it will be useful for everyone. Having said that, I'll now give the floor to the Prosecution and they will have the floor for about three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, General. My name is Daryl Mundis, and along with my colleagues here today, we represent the Prosecution in this case. I know, sir, that you've testified here before, so this is nothing that you haven't experienced, but let me first of all reiterate that my purpose is not in any way to confuse you, and if there is any question that I ask that you don't understand, simply interrupt me and tell me that and I'll either rephrase or reformulate the question so that you do understand. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, I do understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd also, just as an aside, like to say, as a former US naval officer, it's nice to have a former fellow member of the seagoing services in this courtroom since we've had a large number of army people with us. Let me start out by saying -- or asking you some questions about the relationship that you had with General Hadzihasanovic. And I'd like to start out by asking you whether, prior to the time that he assumed command of the 3rd Corps, if you knew General Hadzihasanovic or knew of him prior to the time you began working together in the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know General Hadzihasanovic before that time. I met him when he came to Zenica for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall -- that was in November 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. In November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the initial period when you were getting to know General Hadzihasanovic, did you sit down with him and perhaps discuss or get to become familiar with his background, his military background?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I may start with the first day. It was the beginning of November or the end of October, I'm not quite sure, but at that time we didn't have time to talk about our previous military careers. We had certain tasks to carry out. As I have already said, as the commander of the regional Territorial Defence Staff, it was a very complicated situation. We only discussed our previous military careers very briefly later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, what, to the best of your recollection, you came to learn about General Hadzihasanovic's military career prior to becoming commander of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what General Hadzihasanovic told me, he said he was a member of the 1st Corps. Are you referring to the period up to the beginning of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina? That's the period you're referring to. He said he was in the 1st Corps. At the time, the 1st Corps had already been formed, as far as I know, and that is the position he left when he came to Zenica. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, did you know that General Hadzihasanovic had been with the JNA prior to the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When General Hadzihasanovic arrived, he said that he was a former JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did he tell you or did you at any point in time learn what types of assignments or command positions he had held within the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't discuss this in detail. We didn't discuss our previous positions in the former JNA, but he said that he had been a brigade commander at some time, and just before the war he said that he was in Sarajevo -- he had been in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you know, sir, that he had formerly commanded a military police battalion in the 7th Army of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our first conversations we didn't go that far back. We didn't deal with the posts we had in the former JNA. I didn't inform General Hadzihasanovic of these things nor did he inform me. Perhaps he mentioned this at some point in time but I can't remember having discussed this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that at any other point after the initial period that you and General Hadzihasanovic met each other? Did you ever learn that or did you ever become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember all those details. I really can't remember, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you if you can tell us in general terms about the professional relationship that you developed in late 1992 and throughout the early part of 1993, the professional relationship you developed with the corps commander, General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the time the 3rd Corps was formed, up until the time that General Hadzihasanovic was appointed as a 3rd Corps Commander, we did have contact, and I think we were on quite good terms. He had arrived in the area where I was commander as a professional soldier, and I believed that he understood that I had a high-level command position. He had come -- of course, he had been assigned a certain task, and I was to help him carry out this task. I think that we were on good terms. We treated each other correctly both in military terms -- both from a military point of view and from a personal point of view. We developed a very normal relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the first, say, two to three months that you were assigned as the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, how frequently did you meet with General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when General Hadzihasanovic was appointed as a 3rd Corps Commander, I became his deputy, and we continued to have a normal relationship. I accepted the fact that he was the commander and that I was his deputy. After we had received an order to form the 3rd Corps, I had frequent contact with General Hadzihasanovic. At the time, he had already become the commander. It was necessary to proceed with the establishment of the 3rd Corps, and he wasn't familiar enough with the field, with the units. He didn't know what the structure of the Territorial Defence in that area was. As a soldier, he had general knowledge about plans, about the situation in Sarajevo, but he didn't know anything about the situation in Zenica. So for the first month, throughout the month of December, we frequently went into the field, and we had discussions on a daily basis. We discussed these matters far into the night. We discussed how to form corps units. And at that time, General Hadzihasanovic paid a lot of attention to my suggestions. Naturally, if we have a look at the other months, in January, well, that was a good period, and then later I spent some time in Gornji Vakuf, and we didn't have such frequent contact. In February, combat had started in Busovaca, and we would see each other but not as frequently as in December. But in any event, I think that we did see each other, given the time available. I was always on trips, and I had additional duties, duties other than the duties of deputy commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can I just ask you about the last phrase you said, sir. You said you had additional duties, duties other than the duties of deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. What were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I have already said, in January, I was appointed as a member of the military and political commission for Gornji Vakuf, and I spent some time at the UN headquarters in Gornji Vakuf. In February, I became a member of the Busovaca joint commission, together with representatives of the European Monitoring Mission and representatives of other international organisations, of UNPROFOR. Later, I became a member of the joint commission in Vitez, which was also under the auspices of the European Monitoring Mission. These were my additional duties. And later on, I was a member of the joint command that was formed in Travnik. The composition of these bodies was mixed, but I remained the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. So these were the other duties that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, with respect to these additional duties, this long list of activities that you were involved in, you were representing General Hadzihasanovic on these various commissions or in this role, meeting with international organisations?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was a representative of the 3rd Corps at those meetings or, rather, in those joint commissions, and the commander had given me a significant amount of authority. It wasn't necessary for me to contact him for minor matters. I didn't have a radio link with my commander. I often travelled between Busovaca and Zenica; almost every day. When returning from those trips, I would report to the commander. I would inform him of the work of those commissions and of the results achieved in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So the information that you obtained at these commission meetings or in the field, part of your duties was to relay that information to the corps commander in order to keep him informed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
